item.title: Issue #7: Yuki Matsuri
item.description: Unfortunately, this year the snow festival in Sapporo was canceled because of COVID-19. Luckily, I went to the festival twice when I lived in Japan. The festival started in 1950 with six snow sculptures and now has hundreds of snow and ice sculptures.

item.title: Issue #6: Protests
item.description: On May 25th 2020, George Floyd, a 46-year-old black man was killed by the police in Minneapolis, USA. In the USA, police are often violent especially to minorities. After that people protested in the USA. The protests grew bigger and bigger.

item.title: Issue #5: Pandemic
item.description: In December 2019, a virus started spreading in China. The virus, SARS-CoV-2, is often called COVID-19 or the coronavirus. By February, the virus spread all around the world.

item.title: Issue #4: Flooding In Soma
item.description: On October 12th, Typhoon Hagibis (Typhoon 19) hit Japan. Flooding happened all over Soma. Both of the main rivers in Soma, Koizumi and Uta flooded. Around one quarter of the buildings in Soma flooded.

item.title: Issue #3 School Festivals
item.description: School festivals in Japan are a big deal. They only happen once every three years. They are open to the public and have many different things going on. Each homeroom has their own project.

item.title: Issue #2 UN Climate Action Summit
item.description: Greta Thunberg gave a speech at the UN Climate Action Summit on September 23rd. She told world leaders that she was angry, she said, “You have stolen my dreams and my childhood with your empty words.”

item.title: Issue #1 Soma Nomaoi
item.description: Last month was Soma’s biggest festival: Soma Nomaoi. On Saturday the 27th, there were parades in Soma, Odaka, and Kashima. People from Soso area dressed up as soldiers and samurai. They marched and rode horses in the parades.
